version.changelog: 默认返回最终采集结果，完善异步等待下载与安全恢复；修复空目标误执行、Quick Start、Token 配置和触发路由冲突，并补齐发布前自动化测试

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Dataify-backed DuckDuckGo search helper, but it needs review because its documented command pattern can allow shell command injection and its token handling is broader than necessary.

dimensions.detail: Network access and a Dataify token are expected for this API integration, but the artifact does not clearly declare those scopes, accepts a token via command-line argument, and copies the token into the process environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency bootstrap, remote code retrieval, or tool replacement behavior was found; the package contains markdown instructions, one YAML agent descriptor, and one bundled Python script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions show user-controlled request text interpolated into a shell command in double quotes, which can execute shell substitutions before Python receives the argument; response-handling instructions also conflict between raw passthrough and compact presentation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, or file mutation were found; the docs prefer session-scoped token setup and discuss persistent shell changes only as user-managed configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bundled script parses search requests and posts DuckDuckGo parameters to Dataify, which fits the skill name and workflow, though the short descriptions understate the Dataify third-party API and token dependency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable sending search queries and a Dataify API token to Dataify, avoid putting secrets or private internal text in search requests, and do not invoke the documented command by interpolating untrusted text through a shell; pass arguments safely or require the publisher to fix the invocation and token handling.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Supported in material part: the documented shell invocation with '<user request>' inside double quotes creates command-injection risk; the token command-line option and environment copy are also supported but are credential-exposure issues rather than evidence of malicious payloads.
[TT3] expected: Downgraded: the script sends the Dataify token as an Authorization header to the intended Dataify API endpoint; no evidence showed unrelated environment variables being exfiltrated.
[TP4] expected: Partly supported as under-disclosure: Dataify is disclosed in the title, account policy, and script, but the short descriptions emphasize DuckDuckGo and the code does not independently reject Google/Bing/Yandex wording.
[AE1] unexpected: Not supported after inspection: the referenced Python script was present locally and inspected through line 596.
[LP3] unexpected: Supported as a reviewability concern: the skill relies on local script execution, outbound network access, and environment/token access without visible permission-scope metadata.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported but lower impact: the English and Chinese instructions conflict on whether to return raw stdout unchanged or summarize into compact user-facing results.
[SSD-3] expected: Partly supported: forwarding search text to an external search API is inherent to the purpose, but passing the full request into the parser can over-share incidental sensitive text if users include it.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Not treated as a material security concern for installation; the Chinese localization does not by itself create high-impact authority or hidden behavior.
[EA2] expected: Downgraded: the cited 'never ask' language concerns not asking users to paste tokens into chat and continuing after token configuration; it does not authorize destructive or financial actions.
[SDI-2] expected: Mostly expected for purpose: Dataify account/token onboarding is needed for this provider-backed search flow, though the free-credit CTA is promotional and should be clearer in metadata.
